newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Clashes as Palestinians reject Israeli demands.
newsitem.headline: Clashes as Palestinians reject Israeli demands.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority on Saturday rejected Israeli conditions for resuming peace talks while demonstrators protesting at Israel's building a settlement in Arab East Jerusalem clashed for a tenth day with troops.

Witnesses said at least one Palestinian was wounded when Israeli troops guarding a Jewish shrine at the outskirts of the West Bank Palestinian self-rule enclave of Bethlehem, south of Jerusalem, fired rubber bullets at demonstrators stoning them.
During the protest, demonstrators burned a doll with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's name scrawled on it.
At the outskirts of Bir Zeit village north of the Ramallah West Bank enclave, Israeli soldiers fired tear gas to disperse Palestinians stoning their position.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat told reporters in Gaza on his return from Cairo: "Netanyahu's orders and decisions are escalating the situation in the whole area."
Arafat's adviser Nabil Abu Rdainah said:"What is needed is the implementation of the agreements and the return to the negotiating table without any preconditions or restrictions.
"The new Israeli conditions are not acceptable."
Netanyahu said after meeting U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross on Friday that only a sustained Palestinian crackdown on "terrorism" -- not just a pledge to fight militants -- would salvage peacemaking.

Netanyahu demanded Arafat arrest militants, dismantle guerrilla groups and tighten cooperation between Israeli and Palestinian security forces. He denied Ross asked Israel to make any reciprocal gesture.
Israeli Internal Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani told Israel Television on Saturday that Israel should not rely on the Authority to provide it security.
"Generally, the feeling that we are dependent on them is an awful feeling for the State of Israel -- the great, the grand, the strong -- which has made many wars here," Kahalani said.
Arafat, asked by reporters if Ross in their meeting in Rabat on Thursday, had asked him to calm tensions in Authority areas abutting Israeli army positions where there have been clashes said:
"Yes, they are against the violence, especially the violence of settlement and the Judaization of Jerusalem."

Palestinian-Israeli peace moves plunged into crisis this month after Israel broke ground on the settlement at a hilltop called Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic and Har Homa in Hebrew and after an Islamist suicide bombing in Tel Aviv that killed three Israelis.
Israel says Arafat gave militants the impression they had a green light to carry out attacks. The Authority denies the charge.
Palestinians see building in Jerusalem as preempting negotiations that are to be held on its status in final peace talks which have yet to resume. They demand it be halted.
The White House said on Friday after Ross wound up his two-day emergency mission to the region that it had been "constructive" but that more work was needed to salvage crumbling peace moves.

Thousands of Israeli police, backed by tanks and helicopters, remained on high alert ahead of warnings unrest would peak on Sunday -- the annual "Land Day" when Israeli Arabs stage protests against government confiscation of lands.
Ross said he would report back to U.S. President Bill Clinton and Secretary of State Madeleine Albright before deciding how to tackle the crisis. He called for calm.
